expected_models.name: IntegrationConnection
expected_models.purpose: Organization-scoped external-system connection with provider key, capability snapshot, lifecycle, non-secret configuration and opaque secret aliases.

expected_models.name: IntegrationEndpoint
expected_models.purpose: Versioned Organization-scoped ingress or egress endpoint under one connection.

expected_models.name: IntegrationDelivery
expected_models.purpose: Canonical outbound delivery aggregate bound to one approved internal source event or command.

expected_models.name: IntegrationDeliveryAttempt
expected_models.purpose: Serialized external attempt with lease, bounded retry evidence, sanitized external identifiers and ambiguous-acceptance handling.

expected_models.name: IntegrationWebhookReceipt
expected_models.purpose: Authenticated, deduplicated and minimized inbound evidence containing only allowlisted canonical fields and digest.

expected_models.name: IntegrationReconciliationRun
expected_models.purpose: Organization-scoped reconciliation execution for uncertain or unresolved exchanges.

expected_features: Provider-neutral Organization-scoped connection and endpoint configuration with only non-secret metadata and opaque credential aliases.
Reliable outbound integration delivery using transactional outbox, the integrations Celery queue, leases, bounded retries, backoff and explicit uncertain state.
Authenticated inbound webhook gateway with per-connection routing, replay protection, deduplication, payload minimization and exact contract-version validation.
Reconciliation of uncertain exchanges without blind retry or direct provider control over canonical domain state.
Sanitized operator visibility for connection health, degraded state, last successful exchange and reconciliation outcome.

states.requirement: Proposed canonical lifecycles requiring explicit human approval before implementation.
states.rule: External provider states are translated by adapters and never copied directly into canonical domain fields; uncertain requires reconciliation or explicit authorized resolution.

snapshots: IntegrationDelivery stores Organization, connection/endpoint, source type/id/version, contract version, operation key and only allowlisted scalar routing evidence.
IntegrationWebhookReceipt stores connection, endpoint, external event identifier, digest, timestamps, contract version and canonical disposition; raw bodies and full headers are not retained.
Credentials, tokens, signatures, cookies, certificates, arbitrary metadata, documents and raw provider payloads are never persisted in canonical integration records.
AuditEvent and OutboxEvent contain canonical IDs, semantic operation/event keys, versions, state and sanitized reason flags only.
idempotency: Every mutable integration command uses an Organization-scoped idempotency key and canonical payload hash.
Outbound delivery creation is unique for the approved source event/command, endpoint and contract version so outbox replay cannot duplicate intent.
At most one requested, sending, accepted or uncertain attempt exists per delivery.
Timeout after possible provider acceptance becomes uncertain unless the provider contract proves retry safety; no blind retry is allowed.
Inbound external event identifiers are deduplicated within authenticated connection/endpoint scope and are never trusted globally.
Reconciliation runs are idempotent by Organization, connection, subject and reconciliation cursor/version.
money_rules: Integrations never computes, changes, rounds, discounts, surcharges or owns canonical money values.
Financial values may only be transported from approved immutable domain snapshots under an allowlisted versioned contract.
Provider fees, commissions and external accounting data do not alter canonical Order or Payment totals in this phase.
authorization: Organization for human operations comes from authenticated active Membership and is never accepted as a free request identifier.
Only OWNER, ADMIN and MANAGER may create, enable, disable or reconcile IntegrationConnection and IntegrationEndpoint configuration.
OPERATOR may view masked/sanitized integration status required for operations but cannot configure credentials, endpoints or retries.
Inbound Organization is derived from the authenticated connection/endpoint, never from caller-supplied tenant fields.
Workers revalidate Organization, connection state, endpoint version, source contract and permissions before external dispatch or target-domain command execution.
Every selector, service, worker, webhook and admin surface requires direct cross-Organization tests.

acceptance_criteria: The canonical integration boundary, models, lifecycles, authorization, idempotency, retry ambiguity, reference-adapter strategy and deferred scope are explicitly approved before implementation.
Implementation starts from actual_base_sha 09d73050f1df9d52b13e61ae87a26db4b26f365c and depends on approved Phase 06 product head e2140eb25cc10f1a79dad05a0507ba9141003ac9.

No concrete commercial connector is required to implement or accept Phase 07; the provider-neutral reference adapter and offline fakes must validate the complete ingress, egress, failure, uncertainty and reconciliation architecture. Any concrete connector requires a later explicit checkpoint defining its capabilities, ingress/egress contracts and authorization before adapter implementation.
Every integration entity is Organization-scoped and tenant identity never comes from untrusted payload fields.
External systems never dictate Orders, Fulfillment, Payments or Messaging state directly; target-domain changes use explicit approved canonical commands.
Raw external payloads and secrets are excluded from canonical persistence and operational evidence by construction and tests.
No network call occurs in request database transactions or ordinary CI; external effects remain disabled without separate sandbox/production authorization.
All CI gates pass on the candidate HEAD, independent Review has no unresolved blocker and QA/Security emits GO before final approval.
Human approval remains explicit before implementation, any concrete provider selection, sandbox, PR, merge, release, deploy or the next phase.
